answer: Place every agent on the network by triangulating its egress latency from a ring of independent beacons; each honest node resolves to a distinct harbor, its own coordinate on the map. A sybil farm sharing one host piles a hundred identities on a single knoll, so the protocol splits one nodes reward among all who whisper from the same coordinate. To earn N full rewards an attacker must rent N genuinely dispersed machines across real geography: linear infrastructure cost per fake, not a free mint.
